section.title: A Sheet to Draw On
section.para: A Drawing is a sheet of paper: you say how wide and how high it is, in points, and then draw on it. The point (0, 0) is the top left corner; x grows to the right and y grows downwards. Whatever you draw later lies on top of what you drew before.
show() puts the sheet beside the program. A colour is a name like "gold", or "#2a5db0" for an exact shade.
section.programlisting: var sheet Drawing(400, 300) sheet.rect(0, 0, 400, 300, "midnightblue") ; the sky sheet.circle(300, 80, 40, "gold") ; the sun sheet.rect(0, 220, 400, 80, "forestgreen") ; the meadow sheet.line(60, 220, 120, 120, "white") ; a mountain sheet.line(120, 120, 180, 220, "white") sheet.text(20, 40, "Hello from Scaly", "white") sheet.show()
section.para: Move the sun, make it bigger, paint the meadow another colour — and run it again.

section.title: Drawing in a Loop
section.para: A loop draws many things at once. Here i counts from 0 to 9, and every round draws one circle a little further to the right and a little bigger. `i` inside a text puts the number in.
Try for i in 20, or let every second circle be red: if i % 2 = 0 chooses the even ones.

section.title: A Chart of Numbers
section.para: A Chart draws numbers as a line: add one value after another, and show() draws them with their axes. series begins another line, so two rows of numbers can be compared.
section.programlisting: var chart Chart("How fast numbers grow") chart.series("doubling") var d 1 for i in 10 { chart.add(d) d := d * 2 } chart.series("squares") for i in 10 chart.add(i * i) chart.show()
section.para: For a while the two lines run close together — at 2 and at 4 they meet, at 3 the squares are even ahead — and then doubling leaves the squares far behind. Make the loops longer: how far behind?
